E. Kia Kio and Tree of Life
time limit per test
3 seconds
memory limit per test
256 megabytes
input
standard input
output
standard output

After unlocking the crystal terminal, Kia and Kio discovered the blueprint for the kingdom's forgotten heart: a digital Tree of Life, seeded by the array a1,a2,…,ana1,a2,…,an.

To restore its pulse, they had to weave every possible incarnation of the Tree together. For any continuous segment, Kia would gently select an index ii to plant the root. Trusting her vision, Kio would carefully weave the branches of life — crafting the left subtree from the preceding segment [1,i−1][1,i−1] and the right subtree from the succeeding segment [i+1,n][i+1,n].

Once a Tree of Life bloomed, its vital resonance, f(tree)f(tree), was defined by its bonds. If one were to sever any of the n−1n−1 delicate branches, the Tree would split into two disconnected halves, releasing an energy of X+YX+Y, where XX and YY are the bitwise XOR sums of the array elements remaining in the first and second halves, respectively.

The total power of the Tree, f(tree)f(tree), is the sum of these released energies across all n−1n−1 branches.

Kia wanted to know the ultimate vital force they could awaken. Help them compute the total sum of f(tree)f(tree) across every valid Tree of Life born from their shared bond, modulo 998244353998244353.

Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases tt (1≤t≤1041≤t≤104). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer nn (1≤n≤2⋅1051≤n≤2⋅105) — the size of the array.

The second line contains nn integers a1,a2,…,ana1,a2,…,an (0≤ai<2180≤ai<218).

It is guaranteed that the sum of nn over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅1052⋅105.

Output

For each test case, print a single integer — the total sum of f(tree)f(tree) across all valid Trees of Life, modulo 998244353998244353.

Example
Input
Copy
5
2
1 2
3
1 1 1
3
1 2 3
4
2 1 4 7
5
5 12 9 14 1
Output
Copy
6
10
40
318
2520
Note

For the first test case, n=2n=2 and a=[1,2]a=[1,2]. There are two valid trees that can be constructed: one with a1a1 as the root and a2a2 as the right child, and one with a2a2 as the root and a1a1 as the left child.

In both trees, severing the single branch leaves two components with XOR sums X=1X=1 and Y=2Y=2. Thus, the value for each tree becomes 1+2=31+2=3. The total energy accumulated across both Trees of Life is 3+3=63+3=6.

For the second test case, n=3n=3 and a=[1,1,1]a=[1,1,1].

There are 55 valid trees that can be constructed:

  • Root is 11: {(1,2),(2,3)}{(1,2),(2,3)}, {(1,3),(2,3)}{(1,3),(2,3)};
  • Root is 22: {(1,2),(2,3)}{(1,2),(2,3)};
  • Root is 33: {(1,3),(1,2)}{(1,3),(1,2)}, {(2,3),(1,2)}{(2,3),(1,2)}.

All trees are just a path with three vertices, and severing a single branch leaves two components with XOR sums X=1X=1 and Y=0Y=0. So the value for each tree becomes 22. The total energy accumulated across all five Trees of Life is 5⋅2=105⋅2=10.
